# Hafiz Fabrics - Retail POS and ERP

> Point-of-sale and stock system for a fabric retailer, built on React, TypeScript and Supabase.

Author: Muhammad Tanveer (Full-Stack AI Automation Engineer)
Contact: mtanveertahir66@gmail.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-tanveer-advenno/
Repository: https://github.com/haddindeve/hafiz-fabrics-pos-erp
Source availability: implementation held in a private repository; access on request.

## Summary
A fabric retailer tracked sales and stock on paper. Reconciling what sold against what remained meant counting, and pricing decisions were made without knowing actual margin per item.

A browser-based POS backed by Supabase, so the shop needs no server of its own. The schema is designed for fabric retail specifically - stock measured by length, priced per unit - rather than adapting a generic product-and-quantity model that does not fit how the goods are sold.

## Stack
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Styling: Tailwind CSS, Backend: Supabase (PostgreSQL), Deployment: Static hosting

## Capabilities
- Point-of-sale checkout
- Length-based fabric inventory
- Sales and margin reporting
- Managed Postgres backend with no server to maintain

## Outcomes
- Paper records replaced by live stock and sales figures
- Margin visible per item at the point of pricing

## FAQ
Q: Why Supabase?
A: It provides Postgres, auth and an API without the shop needing to run or maintain a server.

Q: How is fabric stock handled?
A: Stock is tracked by length rather than unit count, matching how fabric is actually bought and sold.

Q: Does it work on existing hardware?
A: It runs in the browser, so any reasonably modern machine or tablet works.

Q: Is the source public?
A: Private repository; access on request.
